chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Sa'id ibn Abi al-Jahm, from Nasr ibn Qabus who said:

I said to Abi al-Hasan the first (peace be upon him): I had asked Aba Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Imam after him and he informed me that it was you, so when he died the people turned away from you to the right and to the left, but I and my companions stuck to you, so inform me about the Imam from your children. He said: My son Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الْأَوَّل: Title for Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْإِمَام: The divinely appointed leader and successor of the Prophet
key_terms.يَمِينًا وَشِمَالًا: Idiom meaning in confusion or in various directions, indicating deviation

ai.seo_question: Who is the Imam after Imam al-Kadhim according to Rijal al-Kashshi?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the critical period of *al-ghubrah* (the minor concealment/transition) where confusion arose after Imam al-Sadiq’s death, yet Nasr ibn Qabus remained a steadfast witness to the designation (*nass*) of Imam al-Kadhim. The Imam’s explicit identification of his son Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon him) as the successor reinforces the Shia doctrine of *nass* (explicit designation) and the continuity of the Imamate through the progeny of Imam al-Husayn. This account serves as a key evidentiary link in establishing the legitimacy of the seventh Imam amidst the fragmentation of the early community.
